title: Arrival: Quba and the camel that knelt
hook: Every morning for days, a whole town walked out to wait for one traveller.

screens.text: **Every morning, they walked out of town to wait.** The Muslims of Madinah had heard the Prophet ﷺ had left Makkah. Day after day they stood at the edge of town until the noon heat sent them home [Bukhari 3906].

**Spotted at last.** One day, just after they'd gone home, a Jewish man on a fort roof saw white-clad travellers coming out of the desert haze. He shouted the news, and the Muslims rushed out to meet him [Bukhari 3906].
bubbles: The people of Madinah had never been so joyful about anything [Bukhari 3925].

screens.prompt: Nobody in Madinah knew his face yet. People asked Abu Bakr who the man with him was. Abu Bakr said: someone who guides me on the way. What did he mean?

options.text: The way of good: the man guiding his life
options.feedback: Right. Listeners thought he meant the road, but Abu Bakr meant the way of good [Bukhari 3911].
Not quite. Many listeners thought so. Abu Bakr meant the man who guided him to good [Bukhari 3911].
Not quite. It was true and careful: he meant the way of good [Bukhari 3911].

screens.text: **First stop: Quba.** He stayed about two weeks at Quba, on the edge of Madinah, with the clan of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf. There he founded a **masjid**, described in the hadith as "founded on piety" [Bukhari 3906; Bukhari 428].
The journey's end, in about 622 CE.

events.title: Waiting
events.text: Madinah's Muslims wait at the edge of town until the heat drives them home [Bukhari 3906].

events.title: Spotted
events.text: A man on a fort roof sees them and calls out [Bukhari 3906].

events.title: Quba
events.text: He stays with Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf and founds a masjid [Bukhari 428].

events.title: Into Madinah
events.text: His camel kneels at the spot that becomes his masjid [Bukhari 3906].

events.title: Year 1
events.text: The Companions later count the Muslim calendar from this journey [Bukhari 3934].

screens.text: **The camel that knelt.** Riding into Madinah, everyone wanted him as their guest. He let his camel walk on. Where it knelt, his masjid would stand. He stayed nearby with Abu Ayyub al-Ansari [Bukhari 3906; Bukhari 428; IslamQA 11575].
bubbles: Everyone wanted to host him. Instead of choosing one family over the rest, he let the camel walk on.

options.feedback: Yes. Day 79 covered this: year 1 is the year of the hijra, about 622 CE.
Not quite. The Companions chose the hijra, not his birth or his death.
Not quite. They chose the move to Madinah as the start of year 1.

screens.text: **A town that waited for a stranger.** He arrived with almost nothing, and a whole city made room for him. Welcoming newcomers is sunnah. A masjid that greets a new convert warmly is walking in Madinah's footsteps.
bubbles: And if you're the newcomer: you're not a burden. You're the guest they've been hoping for.

screens.situation: Aaliyah, a few months Muslim, notices a nervous woman standing near the shoe racks at Jumu'ah, clearly her first time. Aaliyah is shy herself.

options.text: Walk over, say salam, and show her where to go
options.feedback: Yes. A small welcome, like Madinah's. She remembers how that first visit felt.

options.text: Leave it to the regulars; she's still new herself
options.feedback: Not quite. Being new makes her the perfect welcomer. She knows exactly what that moment feels like.

options.text: Wait to see if she comes back next week
options.feedback: Not quite. A first visit is when a welcome matters most. Madinah walked out to meet him.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- He arrived in 622 CE, year 1 of the Muslim calendar [Bukhari 3934; Dar al-Ifta Egypt (seerah part 9); Yaqeen (What Islam Says About Prophet Muhammad)].
- The Muslims of Madinah went out every morning to wait for him until the noon heat drove them back; a Jewish man on a fort roof spotted the travellers and called out [Bukhari 3906].
- He first stayed at Quba with Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf and founded the masjid "founded on piety"; the stay is ten nights in Bukhari 3906 and fourteen in Bukhari 428, so say "about two weeks" [Bukhari 3906; Bukhari 428; IslamQA 11575].
- The people of Madinah had never been so joyful [Bukhari 3925]. Asked who the man with him was, Abu Bakr said someone who guides me on the way, meaning the way of good [Bukhari 3911].
- In Madinah everyone wanted to host him; he let the camel go, it knelt at the place that became his masjid, and he stayed with Abu Ayyub al-Ansari [Bukhari 3906; Bukhari 428; IslamQA 11575].

**Likely questions**
- *"Did they sing Tala'a al-badru when he arrived?"* It's a beloved **nasheed** Muslims have sung for centuries to remember this day; the report that it was sung then has a weak chain [IslamQA 119722]. Enjoy it as a song, not as history. (scholar question Q43)
- *"What is special about Masjid Quba?"* The masjid he founded on arrival, described as founded on piety [Bukhari 3906]. Don't add reward claims that aren't in the bank.
- *"Who was Abu Ayyub?"* A man of Madinah at whose house he stopped and stayed on arrival [Bukhari 428; IslamQA 11575].
- *"How can I help new Muslims feel welcome?"* Simple things: greet them, sit with them, introduce them to one person, follow up. Point to the mentor programme.

**Escalate:** nothing specific.

**Don't**
- Don't present Tala'a al-badru as sung on the day.
- Don't give the exact number of nights at Quba as certain.
